newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NZ says Australia wants "beyond rights" deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NZ says Australia wants "beyond rights" deal.

text.p: New Zealand was satisfied the Australian government wanted to resolve the thorny issue of so-called "beyond rights" for airlines between the two countries, Foreign Minister Don McKinnon said on Thursday.

"We are pretty satisfied the current (Australian) government is treating it very seriously and wants to see it resolved," McKinnon told a news conference following a meeting here with Australian counterpart Alexander Downer.
Australia and New Zealand late last year signed a single aviation agreement allowing the countries' airlines to fly within and between both countries without restriction.
However there are still limits on "beyond rights", preventing New Zealand airlines from taking passengers from Australia to a third country.
The single aviation agreement came two years after the former Australian Labor government suddenly scrapped an earlier agreement just days before it was due to take effect.
"Obviously if something is cancelled unilaterally it leaves a bit of a bad taste and that one did and we do want to see (the issue) out of the way," McKinnon said.
Downer said negotiations on the issue would be taken further by the two countries' Transport Ministers.

They said another market access issue between the two countries, whether or not New Zealand television programmes were eligible for inclusion in Australian content quota on Australian commercial television, was now before the High Court.
McKinnon said New Zealand saw the issue as part of the overall Closer Economic Relationship (CER) services protocol between the two countries.
"We know the attitude taken by some members of the industry here (in Australia) that New Zealand programmes are something of an affront to Australian culture," he said.

"When I mention that to people in New Zealand they just about fall off their barstools choking on their Fosters' (beers) that New Zealand could influence Australian culture by way of television," he said.
However he expressed faith in the CER, saying it was a very wide-ranging agreement that had worked "extraordinarily successfully" for a long time.
